outcome: Nothing published since 26 January 2024 settles Green's conjecture for arbitrary non-hyperelliptic curves: the in-window events are a new proof of the already-known generic odd-genus case (Kemeny, arXiv Feb 2025), a generic positive-characteristic result for a refinement of the conjecture (Kemeny and Wei, arXiv Aug 2025), and two surveys (Park, May 2024; Farkas, Feb 2026), the latter stating that the conjecture 'remains wide open for arbitrary smooth curves'.
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone. (1) For each non-hyperelliptic curve C of genus g: (a) its Clifford index Cliff(C), the minimum over line bundles L with h0(L) >= 2 and h1(L) >= 2 of deg L - 2(h0(L) - 1); (b) the syzygy data of C embedded by its canonical bundle K_C, i.e. the Koszul cohomology groups K_{p,q}(C,K_C), in particular how far linear syzygies extend (the vanishing of K_{p,2} or K_{p,1} below a threshold). (2) The claim that (a) is determined by (b): the Clifford index is read off from the extent of linear syzygies, in the standard form K_{p,2}(C,K_C) = 0 if and only if p < Cliff(C). Parts that must each be accounted for: (i) the direction that is classically attributed to Green and Lazarsfeld (the sources I read describe it as proved; I did not open the original); (ii) the converse direction for all non-hyperelliptic curves, which the sources I read call open. The field is not fixed by the bullet. The literature works over C or over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero, and the statement's wording does not say which. Sources index the Koszul groups differently (K_{p,2} in some, K_{i,1} in others, and a g-p-2 variant in Teixidor's form); the judging pass should use the standard form given here.

events.what_happened: Hirschowitz and Ramanan, 'New evidence for Green's conjecture on syzygies of canonical curves', arXiv alg-geom/9707017. Abstract: 'We prove that two weakened forms of Green's conjectures for canonical curves are equivalent when the genus g is odd.' The generic and specific forms are named in later sources (Teixidor's restatement, seen in search results), not in this abstract. Published in Annales scientifiques de l'Ecole normale superieure in 1998 according to a numdam listing seen in search results; that listing was not opened.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only as read. Journal publication 1998 per the numdam listing (not opened).
events.delivers: For odd genus only, the generic form of Green's conjecture and the specific form (curves of maximal Clifford index satisfy it) are equivalent. This is a reduction, not a verification of either form.
events.remains: Both forms, for every genus; the even-genus case is not addressed in the abstract; the full conjecture for all curves.

checked_by.who: Annales scientifiques de l'Ecole normale superieure (refereed journal)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the 1998 publication
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for publication in 1998 (per the numdam listing; referee reports not visible)

events.direction: Reduces the generic odd-genus question to the specific one. Cuts neither way on the conjecture itself.

events.what_happened: Teixidor i Bigas, 'Green's Conjecture for the generic canonical curve', arXiv math/9806017. Abstract: 'We prove that the generic curve of genus g satisfies Green's conjecture.' No journal version found. The paper body was not read.
events.delivers: As claimed in the abstract: the generic curve of every genus satisfies Green's conjecture. The abstract does not state a characteristic; the claim is conflicting with later sources (see doubts and disputes).
events.remains: Non-generic curves, all genera, if the claim is accepted.
events.doubts: Conflicting framing in later sources. Voisin's 2005 abstract (arXiv math/0301359, opened) says earlier results 'proved the conjecture for generic curves of genus g with fixed gonality d when d >= g/3, except possibly for generic curves of odd genus', and her paper proves the odd-genus generic case. A search result restating Teixidor's own work says it 'settles the whole question for odd genus', which does not match Voisin's account. I did not read the 1998 body or any journal version, so I cannot say which reading the paper supports.
events.direction: If accepted, cuts in favour of the conjecture for generic curves of every genus.

events.what_happened: Voisin, 'Green's generic syzygy conjecture for curves of even genus lying on a K3 surface', arXiv math/0205330, first posted 31 May 2002 (single version). The fetched abstract text (paraphrased by the fetch tool) says the new approach allows the generic case to be proved for gonality in the range g/3 + 1 <= gon(C) <= g/2 + 1; I could not read the exact abstract wording. Journal: Journal of the European Mathematical Society 4 (2002) 363-404, per an EMS listing seen in search results (not opened).
events.delivers: Generic curves of even genus, via K3 surfaces, for the gonality range stated in the abstract (as paraphrased). Together with the odd-genus paper below, this is the standard credit for the generic case.
events.remains: Non-generic curves; the odd-genus generic case (see the 2003 event); the full conjecture.

checked_by.who: Journal of the European Mathematical Society (refereed journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2002 per the EMS listing seen in search results (not opened)

checked_by.who: Gavril Farkas (author of the 2026 survey arXiv 2602.22493)
checked_by.qualification: Active researcher in syzygies of curves
checked_by.what_they_did: Cites and credits Voisin's proof of the general case ('Green's Conjecture for general curves has been famously proved by Voisin'). Credit, not an independent re-check.

events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture for generic curves of even genus in the stated gonality range.

events.what_happened: Voisin, 'Green's canonical syzygy conjecture for generic curves of odd genus', arXiv math/0301359, first posted 30 January 2003; revised 5 Feb 2003, 16 May 2003, 22 Oct 2004. Abstract: 'We prove the Green conjecture for generic curves of odd genus.' Proves K_{k,1}(X,K_X) = 0 for generic X of genus 2k+1, using K3 surfaces of Picard rank 2. Journal: Compositio Mathematica 141 (2005) 1163-1190, per the arXiv journal reference.
events.revisions: v2 5 Feb 2003; v3 16 May 2003; v4 22 Oct 2004. Journal reference Compos. Math. 141 (2005).
events.delivers: Generic curves of odd genus, all gonalities. With the even-genus paper, this is the generic form of Green's conjecture for all genera in characteristic zero, which the 2026 survey and the Wikipedia page for Clifford's theorem both credit to Voisin.
events.remains: Every non-generic smooth curve of every genus. The full conjecture.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2005 (journal reference on the arXiv page)
Worked through this result and gave a new proof of it (see event kemeny-2025-odd-genus)

events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture for generic odd-genus curves.

events.what_happened: Sagraloff, 'Special linear series and syzygies of canonical curves of genus 9', arXiv math/0605758, first posted 30 May 2006. Abstract (as read): gives 'a complete description of the syzygies' of irreducible nonsingular canonical curves of genus 9, and 'a collection of all possible Betti tables'. The abstract does not name Green's conjecture. A search snippet describing the paper as a German-language thesis and claiming it establishes Green's conjecture for g <= 9 was not verified.
events.delivers: A genus-9 instance: a full syzygy and Betti-table description for canonical curves of genus 9. Whether this yields Green's conjecture for genus 9 is not stated in the abstract and would need the body.
events.remains: All other genera; the conjecture as a universal claim over all curves.
events.direction: Instance-level: consistent with the conjecture for genus 9 if the Betti tables match the predicted pattern (not checked).

events.what_happened: Colombo, Farkas, Verra and Voisin, 'Syzygies of Prym and paracanonical curves of genus 8', arXiv 1612.01026, first posted 3 December 2016. Abstract: 'we present three geometric proofs of the surprising failure of the Prym-Green Conjecture in genus 8.' Published Epijournal de Geometrie Algebrique 1 (2017), epiga:2602.
events.revisions: Journal publication 2017 per the arXiv journal reference.
events.delivers: The Prym-Green conjecture, an analogue for paracanonical/Prym curves, fails in genus 8 at level 2. This is a different question from Green's conjecture for canonical curves.
events.remains: Green's conjecture for canonical curves is not touched by this result.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2017 per the arXiv journal reference

events.direction: Counterexample to an analogue (Prym-Green), not to Green's conjecture as stated. Recorded because the analogue is the closest published counterexample-type result.
events.object: Three geometric constructions (per the abstract) showing that the Prym-Green conjecture fails for genus 8 at level 2. Not read in detail; the constructions are not described in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Kemeny, 'The Geometric Syzygy Conjecture in Even Genus', arXiv 1907.07553, first posted 17 July 2019. Abstract: 'We prove the Geometric Syzygy Conjecture for generic canonical curves of even genus.' The abstract refers to Green's classical result on rank-four quadrics and does not name Green's conjecture.
events.delivers: Geometric Syzygy Conjecture for generic canonical curves of even genus. This is a refinement of Green's conjecture (the linear syzygy spaces are spanned by minimal-rank syzygies), a different question, not Green's conjecture itself.
events.remains: Green's conjecture itself; the Geometric Syzygy Conjecture for non-generic curves.
events.direction: Analogue (refinement), different question. Cuts in favour of the refinement for generic even-genus curves.

events.what_happened: Aprodu and Farkas, 'Green's conjecture for curves on arbitrary K3 surfaces', Compositio Mathematica (DOI 10.1112/S0010437X10005099). The year 2011 comes from the PDF metadata creation date (10 May 2011) and was not confirmed from the journal page. The main theorem could not be read from the PDF. The 2026 Farkas survey (section 5.1, opened) says the paper 'cites a proof that all curves on K3 surfaces satisfy the conjecture'.
events.delivers: Per the 2026 survey's description: Green's conjecture for every smooth curve lying on a K3 surface, with the exact Picard-lattice hypotheses not read.
events.remains: Curves that do not lie on a K3 surface; the full conjecture.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published, per the Cambridge link (not verified in full)

events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture for K3 curves, a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Bopp and Schreyer, 'A version of Green's conjecture in positive characteristic', arXiv 1803.10481, first posted 28 March 2018. Abstract: they 'formulate a refined version of Green's conjecture' and run experiments with a Macaulay2 package that constructs random canonically embedded curves of genus g <= 15 over small finite fields. The refined version concerns a Schicho-Schreyer-Weimann conjecture that 'conjecturally also holds in positive characteristic'.
events.delivers: A refined conjecture for positive characteristic and computational evidence for genera up to 15 over small finite fields. Not a proof for the problem as stated, and not a counterexample to it.
events.remains: Everything in the problem statement; the refinement is a different question.

machine_checked.system: Macaulay2 (Bopp-Schreyer package for random canonical curves)

events.direction: Refined positive-characteristic version and computational evidence. Does not cut either way on the problem as stated. The small-characteristic failures are recorded in the next event.

events.what_happened: Reports of Green's conjecture failing in small positive characteristic. The 2026 Farkas survey (arXiv 2602.22493, section 5.2-5.3 as read) says: 'Schreyer observed computationally that Green's Conjecture fails for every curve in low characteristic for infinitely many genera. The first counterexamples are g=7 with char 2, and g=9 with char 3.' The survey gives no date. A search snippet for arXiv 1804.08011 (2018, not opened) says the genus 7 and genus 9 cases are rigorously proven. The earliest dated source I read that discusses these computations is Bopp and Schreyer (2018), but its abstract does not state the failures. So the date given here is an upper bound taken from that paper.
events.delivers: As quoted: Green's conjecture fails in characteristic 2 for genus 7 and characteristic 3 for genus 9, and per the survey's wording, in low characteristic for infinitely many genera. Consequently the statement is false over those fields.
events.remains: Characteristic zero and large positive characteristic are not affected by these examples as quoted.

checked_by.qualification: Active researcher in syzygies of curves
checked_by.what_they_did: Reports Schreyer's computational findings in section 5.2-5.3 of the survey. Reporting, not independent verification.

machine_checked.system: Macaulay2 computations (Schreyer's; Bopp-Schreyer package for the 2018 experiments)

events.doubts: The 'rigorous' status of the genus 7 and genus 9 failures rests on a snippet for arXiv 1804.08011 that I did not open. The survey's wording is computational. Whether the bullet is meant over C or over arbitrary fields is not fixed by the statement.
events.direction: Cuts against the statement in the specified small characteristics (counterexamples). Does not touch characteristic zero.
events.object: Canonical curves of genus 7 in characteristic 2 and of genus 9 in characteristic 3, for which the predicted Betti pattern fails (per the survey, computational). The survey does not describe the curves. The 2026 survey and the search snippet both note that for genus 11, 13 and 15 the comparison with the generic Betti numbers is unknown. The examples are from computer-generated random curves, not an explicit construction.

events.what_happened: Estu, Im, Manning, Michaels, Pasko, Rulla and Wijesinghe, 'Examples relating to Green's conjecture in low characteristics and genera', arXiv 1912.05998, first posted 12 December 2019. Abstract: 'Generic Green's conjecture is verified for genera 9 and 10 for characteristics 2, 5, 7, and 11.' A search snippet (not verified) describes Betti diagrams for genera 9 to 14 over characteristics 2 to 11, computed with Groebner bases, from a 2002 REU project.
events.delivers: Computational verification of the generic form of Green's conjecture for genera 9 and 10 in characteristics 2, 5, 7 and 11. These are finitely many instances of a generic claim in fixed positive characteristics.
events.remains: Characteristic zero; all other genera; the non-generic conjecture.

machine_checked.system: Computer algebra (system not named in the abstract; Groebner-basis computations per an unverified snippet)

events.direction: Consistent with the generic conjecture for the listed instances. Not against it.

events.what_happened: Aprodu, Farkas, Papadima, Raicu and Weyman, 'Koszul modules and Green's conjecture', arXiv 1810.11635, first posted 27 October 2018 (v2 23 Nov 2018; v3 29 May 2019). Comments field: 'to appear in Invent. Math.'; DOI 10.1007/s00222-019-00894-1. Abstract: a vanishing result for finite-length Koszul modules, used to establish Green's conjecture for every g-cuspidal rational curve over an algebraically closed field, in characteristic zero or characteristic at least (g+2)/2. Consequently the general canonical curve of genus g satisfies the conjecture in that range; also a new proof of Voisin's theorems in characteristic zero.
events.delivers: Green's conjecture for g-cuspidal rational curves, and for general canonical curves, in characteristic zero or at least (g+2)/2.
events.remains: Non-general, non-cuspidal curves in every characteristic; general curves in characteristic below (g+2)/2.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted per the arXiv comments field ('to appear in Invent. Math.'); the published version was not opened
Gives a second, geometric proof of the generic case building on these methods

events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture for general curves in the stated characteristic range, and for g-cuspidal rational curves.

events.what_happened: Raicu and Sam, 'Bi-graded Koszul modules, K3 carpets, and Green's conjecture', arXiv 1909.09122, first posted 19 September 2019; v2 2 August 2021. Journal reference: Compositio Mathematica 158 (2022), 33-56. Abstract: confirms an Eisenbud-Schreyer conjecture on the characteristics in which the generic statement of Green's conjecture holds; proves the Canonical Ribbon Conjecture 'over a field of characteristic zero or at least equal to the Clifford index'. Per the 2026 survey, the bound matches Eisenbud-Schreyer's except for g = 2p+1 in characteristic p, where it is better by one.
events.delivers: Generic Green's conjecture in characteristic zero and in characteristic at least the Clifford index bound (per abstract). A search snippet also says it recovers Voisin's generic results for each gonality; not verified in the abstract.
events.remains: Non-generic curves; the full conjecture.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2022 (journal reference on the arXiv page)
Describes the bound and the one exception (section 5.2)

events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture for generic curves in the stated characteristic range.

events.what_happened: Yi Wei, 'Generic Green's Conjecture and Generic Geometric Syzygy Conjecture in Positive Characteristic', arXiv 2109.12187, first posted 24 September 2021. Abstract: a new proof of the generic Green's conjecture for characteristic p >= (g+4)/2 (g >= 3). Latest version (v4, 13 May 2025) also treats a case of the Geometric Syzygy Conjecture for even genus under p > g, per a search listing of the v4 abstract (not opened).
events.revisions: v2 16 Oct 2021; v3 30 May 2023; v4 13 May 2025 (retitled).
events.delivers: Generic Green's conjecture in characteristic p >= (g+4)/2. The bound is weaker than the (g+2)/2 bound of AFPRW (2018), which the paper itself notes. The even-genus Geometric Syzygy case (v4) is a different question.
events.remains: Non-generic curves; characteristic below (g+4)/2.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture for generic curves in positive characteristic.

events.what_happened: Jinhyung Park, 'Syzygies of tangent developable surfaces and K3 carpets via secant varieties', arXiv 2212.07584, first posted 15 December 2022 (one version listed). Published in Algebra & Number Theory 19:5 (2025), DOI 10.2140/ant.2025.19.1029 (per a search listing). The ANT PDF I fetched returned only cover text and bookmarks, so the journal details are from the listing. Abstract: 'a quick proof of Green's conjecture for general curves of genus g' in characteristic zero or at least floor((g-1)/2).
events.delivers: A geometric proof of the generic case of Green's conjecture in characteristic zero or at least floor((g-1)/2). Not new scope: the generic case was already known from Voisin.
events.remains: Non-generic curves; the full conjecture.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2025 (per the search listing; the PDF text was not readable)

events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture for generic curves; a re-proof of a known case.

events.what_happened: Gavril Farkas, 'Difference varieties and the Green-Lazarsfeld Secant Conjecture', arXiv 2307.14157, first posted 26 July 2023; revised 16 June 2024 (v2, described as final, to appear in the Epijournal volume dedicated to Claire Voisin). Abstract: the Secant Conjecture is 'a generalization of Green's Conjecture' from K_C to arbitrary line bundles; it is established for curves of genus g in the divisorial case.
events.revisions: v2 16 Jun 2024 (in window). Journal publication not verified.
events.delivers: The Secant Conjecture for arbitrary line bundles in the divisorial case. A different question: a generalization of Green's conjecture. The abstract does not claim the K_C instance, which is Green's conjecture, in the divisorial case.
events.remains: Green's conjecture itself (not claimed here); the Secant Conjecture for non-divisorial line bundles.
events.direction: Analogue (generalization), different question. Does not settle Green's conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Jinhyung Park, arXiv 2405.18022, submitted 28 May 2024. Survey of recent work on syzygies of algebraic varieties (search listing gives the title 'Syzygies of algebraic varieties through symmetric products of algebraic curves'). The abstract lists Green's conjecture on syzygies of canonical curves among its topics and says all results considered were proven using the geometry of symmetric products. No new theorem on Green's conjecture is claimed in the abstract. The body was not read.
events.delivers: No new result on Green's conjecture is claimed in the abstract. It is a survey.
events.remains: All of the problem as stated.
events.direction: No direction: no new result.

events.what_happened: Michael Kemeny, 'A proof of generic Green's conjecture in odd genus', arXiv 2502.09735. First arXiv version 13 February 2025; v2 22 June 2025; v3 27 June 2025; v4 10 December 2025. Abstract: 'a new proof of Voisin's theorem on Green's conjecture for generic curves of odd genus', avoiding the heavy computation of earlier proofs. Published Epijournal de Geometrie Algebrique 9 (2025), epiga:15338, accepted 28 July 2025, published 12 December 2025. The EPIGA page gives 'Submitted: 6 March 2025', which is later than the arXiv v1 date; per section 5.1 I use the arXiv date. Main result (Theorem 2.8, read in the HTML): for a K3 surface of Picard rank 2 with a specified polarisation and a smooth rational curve, K_{k-1,2}(X,L) = 0. The paper states the application to generic odd-genus curves.
events.revisions: v2 22 Jun 2025; v3 27 Jun 2025; v4 10 Dec 2025 (89 KB, the substantive revision per the listing). Journal: EPIGA 9 (2025), published 12 Dec 2025.
events.delivers: A new proof of the generic odd-genus case of Green's conjecture, which Voisin proved in 2005. No new genus, gonality or characteristic is covered. The scope is entirely inside the already-known generic case.
events.remains: Every non-generic smooth curve; the full conjecture. Even-genus generic is already known (Voisin 2002, event voisin-2002-even-genus).

checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed journal; the EPIGA page does not name editors or referees. The author thanks 'the referee' in the acknowledgements.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the generic odd-genus case. Settles nothing beyond what Voisin (2005) settled.

events.what_happened: Michael Kemeny and Peter Yi Wei, 'The Geometric Syzygy Conjecture in Positive Characteristic', arXiv 2509.00844, v1 31 August 2025 (only version listed). Main theorem (Theorem 1.1, read in the HTML): the Geometric Syzygy Conjecture holds for general curves of genus g >= 4 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p >= 2g - 4. The Geometric Syzygy Conjecture says linear syzygy spaces K_{i,1}(C,K_C) are spanned by syzygies of minimal rank i+1. Introduction: Green's conjecture is 'still in general open'; Voisin settled the general case over C.
events.delivers: The Geometric Syzygy Conjecture, a refinement of Green's conjecture, for general curves of genus g >= 4 in characteristic p >= 2g - 4. Not Green's conjecture itself, and restricted to general curves.
events.remains: Green's conjecture for non-general curves; the Geometric Syzygy Conjecture for non-general curves; characteristic p < 2g - 4.
events.direction: Different question (refinement, general curves, positive characteristic). Does not cut on Green's conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Gavril Farkas, 'Syzygies and Koszul modules in geometry', arXiv 2602.22493, v1 26 February 2026, v2 28 February 2026. Survey for the 2025 Summer Research Institute in Algebraic Geometry. States the status of Green's conjecture: 'remains wide open for arbitrary smooth curves' (section 5.1), and that Voisin proved the general case (section 1). Gives Koszul-module proofs of the generic case in characteristic zero or at least (g+2)/2 (Theorem 5.4 as read in the first excerpt). The second excerpt gives the Eisenbud-Schreyer bound of (g-1)/2. Lists open questions 5.5, 5.7, 5.8, 6.3 and 6.4, of which 6.4 asks whether a version of Green's conjecture should hold for all smooth curves of genus g.
events.revisions: v2 28 Feb 2026 (listing). PDF text was not extractable, so I used the HTML rendering.
events.delivers: No new theorem on Green's conjecture in the parts I read. It is a status statement by an expert: the full conjecture is open.
events.remains: The full conjecture.
events.direction: No direction: status statement only.

disputes.summary: Teixidor i Bigas (arXiv math/9806017, 1998) states the generic curve of every genus satisfies Green's conjecture. Voisin's odd-genus paper (arXiv math/0301359; Compos. Math. 2005) says earlier results covered generic curves only for fixed gonality d >= g/3 and left generic odd genus open; the Wikipedia page for Clifford's theorem and the 2026 survey credit Voisin with the generic case. No source I read reconciles the 1998 claim with Voisin's account.

summary: Searched 41 times (list below) and opened the sources cited. Since 26 January 2024 the only events are: Park's survey (arXiv 2405.18022, May 2024, no new result claimed); Kemeny's new proof of the generic odd-genus case, which Voisin proved in 2005 (arXiv 2502.09735, Feb 2025; published in Epijournal de Geometrie Algebrique 9, Dec 2025); Kemeny and Wei's result on the Geometric Syzygy Conjecture, a refinement of Green's conjecture, for general curves in characteristic at least 2g-4 (arXiv 2509.00844, Aug 2025, not in a journal as far as I found); and Farkas's 2026 survey (arXiv 2602.22493), which says the conjecture 'remains wide open for arbitrary smooth curves' and poses it as open question 6.4. None of these moves the full conjecture. The Kemeny result and the Kemeny-Wei result are inside the known generic case or are about a different question. Before the window, the generic case was settled in characteristic zero by Voisin (arXiv 2002 and 2003; Compositio 2005), re-proved with Koszul modules (Aprodu, Farkas, Papadima, Raicu and Weyman, 2018; Raicu and Sam, 2019), with positive-characteristic extensions (Wei 2021; Park 2022). Partial results exist for K3 curves (Aprodu and Farkas), genus 9 (Sagraloff 2006, from the abstract only), and computationally for genera 9 and 10 in some small characteristics (Estu et al. 2019). The main counterexample-type finding is the failure of the conjecture in small positive characteristic (genus 7 in characteristic 2, genus 9 in characteristic 3; survey section 5.2-5.3, computational). The bullet does not fix a field, so this must be read against its intended setting. A close call: Teixidor's 1998 claim of the full generic case conflicts with Voisin's later account, and I could not resolve it from the sources. A second close call: whether the Prym-Green failure in genus 8 (Colombo, Farkas, Verra, Voisin, 2016) bears on this bullet. I recorded it as an analogue with a different question. No AI involvement was found. Searches for AI and Green's conjecture (lab announcements, AI-result trackers, Erdos-problem lists, FrontierMath Open Problems, Lean formalisations, DeepMind and Axiom systems, OpenAI announcements) returned nothing on this problem. The authors of the in-window papers I read disclose no AI or tool use beyond NSF funding and a refereeing thanks; the Farkas survey acknowledgement was not seen in full. Wikipedia: the 'Green's conjecture' title redirects to 'Clifford's theorem on special divisors', whose Green's conjecture section calls the general-curve case proved by Voisin and 'the conjecture for arbitrary curves' open; the fetch reported a last edit on 5 December 2024. The list of unsolved problems still carries this bullet with no solved marking, and no 'solved since 2015' entry mentions it. Notation: sources index the Koszul groups differently (K_{p,2} vs K_{i,1}, and a g-p-2 variant); I used the standard form stated in problem_asks.
competing_reading: Read the 1998 Teixidor claim, the 2002/2003 Voisin papers and the 2018-2019 Koszul-module and ribbon papers as completing the generic case in characteristic zero. Then the problem is 'solved for generic curves' and the open part is the non-generic remainder. The in-window events add re-proofs (Kemeny 2025) and a refinement for general curves (Kemeny-Wei 2025), which on that reading leave the status unchanged. Alternatively, read the small-characteristic failures as making the statement false outright, which would be the answer if the bullet is meant over arbitrary fields. Both readings agree on the in-window fact: nothing new in scope since January 2024.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The 1998 Teixidor paper and any journal version, and whether Voisin's 2005 paper or later work addresses it. (2) The intended field of the bullet, which decides whether the small-characteristic failures count against the statement. (3) The arXiv 1804.08011 claim that the genus 7 and genus 9 failures are rigorous, which I did not open. (4) The body of Sagraloff's genus-9 paper, to see whether Green's conjecture for genus 9 is stated. (5) A post-October 2026 search of arXiv math.AG for 'Green's conjecture' in titles and abstracts, and a check of the open questions in the Farkas 2026 survey (particularly 6.4). The search index covers recent months poorly, so this is not ruled out.
